record.paper_title: FPT Suspects and Tough Customers: Open Problems of Downey and Fellows
record.original_question: Given an undirected red/blue bipartite graph G = (R, B, E) and a positive integer k, is there a nonempty subset R' of R of size at most k such that every vertex in B has an even number of neighbors in R'?

evidence.quote: Question: Is there a non-empty set of at most k vertices R ⊆ R, such that each member of B has an even number of neighbors in R?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G = (R ∪ B, E) be a finite undirected bipartite graph with vertex parts R ("red") and B ("blue") and edge set E ⊆ R × B, and let k be a positive integer. The Even Set problem asks: does there exist a nonempty subset R' ⊆ R with |R'| ≤ k such that for every vertex b ∈ B, the number of neighbors of b lying in R' (i.e., |{r ∈ R' : (r,b) ∈ E}|) is even?

Determine the parameterized complexity of this decision problem when parameterized by k. In particular, is Even Set fixed-parameter tractable in k, or is it W[1]-hard (or harder) under the standard parameterized-complexity hierarchy?
artifact.status_search_result: Bhattacharyya, Bonnet, Egri, Ghoshal, Karthik C. S., Lin, Manurangsi, and Marx (ICALP 2018; J. ACM 2021) proved that k-Even Set is W[1]-hard under randomized reductions, assuming Gap-ETH. Thus the problem is unlikely to be FPT, but a deterministic reduction and full resolution (e.g., W[1]-hardness without randomization, or stronger hardness) remain open.

status_evidence.title: Parameterized Intractability of Even Set and Shortest Vector Problem
status_evidence.snippet: k-Even Set is W[1]-hard under randomized reductions; resolves a long-standing open question of Downey and Fellows.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is W[1]-hard under randomized reductions, so not FPT unless FPT = W[1] under randomized reductions.

status_evidence.title: Parameterized Intractability of Even Set and Shortest Vector Problem from Gap-ETH (arXiv:1803.09717)
status_evidence.snippet: We show that k-Even Set is W[1]-hard under randomized reductions assuming Gap-ETH.
status_evidence.claim: Randomized W[1]-hardness of Even Set parameterized by k.
